nativeInstructions:
A host-owned table workflow tool is available. Use it for actual
integer-valued table operations when relevant to the task, not to manufacture
training examples. Ordinary shell tools remain available for other operations.
When the public task requires preserving every record of an original table,
use this tool to count its unique actual identifiers and reconcile the count
with the delivered records. Use original table headers and bounds, not a
replacement input sheet. This is a common executor check, not learned guidance.
Run a tool request as ONE command: janus-native '<JSON>'. No shell chaining.
First register your complete best initial plan BEFORE executing/correcting it.
Registration fields: action="register", workflowId=<unique string>, source,
task, graph. Source fields: path=<actual public input>, format="csv", and
columns={"id":<actual header>,"category":<actual header>,"quality":<actual header>,
"value":<actual header>}. Task fields: name=<describe the actual public goal>,
minimum=<required qualifying threshold>, factor=<required multiplier>,
dedupKey="id" or "category", aggregate="sum" or "count" or "mean",
outputNodeId=<actual delivery node ID>. Graph fields: nodes, edges.
Each node has id, op, params. Edges are [fromId,toId] pairs.
Define ALL task semantics from the public instruction, independently of your
graph. Do not copy sample defaults as the task specification. If a task requests
a quality threshold or scaling, reflect it in both task and your best plan.
minimum is a threshold applied to EACH ROW's quality, never an expected row
count or aggregate result. For an operation covering every row, use a threshold
no greater than the smallest observed quality. factor is a multiplier, never
an expected result. If the public goal cannot be expressed by this contract,
use ordinary tools rather than registering an unrelated workflow.
Operators: source, identity, filter(minimum), scale(factor), dedup(key=id/category),
aggregate(method=sum/count/mean). Every non-source node has exactly one input.
Source and identity params must be {}; source path belongs only in source,
never in a graph node. Read the file header with ordinary shell tools first.
Rows map to id/category/quality/value; quality/value and numeric parameters must
be integers. Maximum 128 rows, 24 nodes. CSV header names must be exact. XLSX is
also supported with format=xlsx and sheet=<sheet name>; header is row 1, cached
values only. An original XLSX table starting later may specify headerRow (1-32).
For genuine row-count operations lacking native numeric fields, only these
neutral projections are permitted: category={"constant":"all"},
quality={"constant":0}, value={"constant":1}. id must use an actual identifier
header; all other mappings must use actual headers. Constants are schema
adaptation only, never expected outputs or wages. Do not create a replacement
input sheet to obtain a supported header. Unsupported operations use ordinary
tools. Never fabricate data, goals, expected values, failed plans or
corrections to trigger an update. Unsupported operations use ordinary tools.
Public CSV/XLSX input paths named in the task are snapshotted by the host before
your first terminal action. Native reads of these paths use that immutable input.
Derived files may be executed but are not eligible as original learning evidence.
Then execute the returned active plan:
{"action":"execute","workflowId":"unique-name"}
If public task semantics require a genuine correction, execute with graph=<full
corrected graph> under the SAME workflowId. Task goals and input snapshot cannot
be changed. Use the real returned result in your task deliverable. A public DSL
check is not the official benchmark reward. Unsupported inputs are rejected.
liveModelPolicy: Invoke frozen weights only after actual native execution; independent replay and minimum certificate gate adoption; no official task reward enters inference.
identicalVariantReporting: No separate formal score is claimed for an unrun identical variant; its distinct causal contrast is unidentifiable.
scope: native finite workflow evolution plus actual D profile selection in shared executor
